analysis: Chronic use of NSAIDs is a well-known risk factor for the development of peptic ulcers due to the inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis, which is crucial for maintaining the protective mucosal barrier in the gastrointestinal tract. Misoprostol, a prostaglandin analog, is specifically indicated for the prevention and treatment of NSAID-induced peptic ulcers as it not only provides mucosal protection but also promotes healing of existing ulcers. While Esomeprazole is effective in reducing gastric acid secretion and can be used in the management of peptic ulcers, it is not the first-line treatment specifically for NSAID-induced ulcers. Other options like Pirenzepine and Loratadine are not relevant to the treatment of peptic ulcers. Therefore, based on the consensus in the medical community regarding the management of NSAID-induced peptic ulcers, Misoprostol is the most appropriate choice. The reasoning aligns with established guidelines and clinical practice, leading to a high confidence in this conclusion.
